questions.text: Which end-user market segment is the primary customer today — LLM KVCache, M→N elasticity, RL parameter rearrangement, checkpoint, or microservice state — and which are aspirational? (Product Owner, Domain Expert)

Why was DataSystem built — was it extracted to accelerate a specific in-house LLM-inference product, to replace an external cache (Redis/Alluxio-like), or as a general openYuanrong platform component? (Product Owner)
What success metrics define 'working well' — what are the target SLOs (e.g. p99 Get latency, throughput, cache hit ratio) that would count as success? (Product Owner)
Given heterogeneous/NPU paths are optional, is KVCache-for-inference first among equals, or is another scenario the ordering driver for the use-case roadmap? (Product Owner)
On SetParam.ttlSecond expiry, is the key hard-deleted or merely eligible for eviction? Do reads after expiry fail or miss silently? (Product Owner, Domain Expert)
What is the runtime contract/coupling between DataSystem and the other two openYuanrong repos (runtime, function system)? (Product Owner)
What are the mandated review/branching/release rules — required approvals, protected branches, release cadence, merge ownership? (Architect, Operations)
Why elect a master among workers via ETCD CAS rather than run a dedicated master tier — what trade-offs (operational simplicity vs. blast radius) drove this design? (Architect)

Why is service traffic on a custom ZeroMQ RPC framework instead of the already-linked gRPC — was it latency, shared-memory/UDS integration, or payload control, and what alternatives were considered? (Architect)
Why maintain both ETCD and Metastore coordination backends — which is recommended for which deployment, and is Metastore meant to eventually replace external ETCD? (Architect, Operations)
Where are architecture decisions recorded — is there an external ADR store, or are decisions only in design docs or people's heads? (Architect)
What target SLOs (RTO/RPO, p99 latency, availability %) are the code knobs (60s/300s timeouts, 100 MB no-copy threshold, etc.) meant to satisfy? (Architect, Product Owner)

What is the required security posture — is plaintext-by-default acceptable (trusted-network assumption)? Are compliance frameworks in scope? What is the threat model (single-tenant vs. multi-tenant)? (Architect, Operations, Product Owner)
When performance and reliability conflict (e.g. latency vs. availability during failover), which ranks first — and does that ordering change per use-case? (Architect, Product Owner)
Perf tests exist but assert no numeric bar — what regression magnitude should fail a build, making performance a verifiable acceptance criterion? (Architect)
When a slow consumer fills cacheCapacity, does the producer block, drop, or error — what is the intended slow-consumer contract? (Architect, Domain Expert)
What is the recommended default WriteMode and ConsistencyType (PRAM vs. Causal) per scenario, and why is PRAM the base case (=0)? (Architect, Domain Expert)
What are the validated scale limits — max nodes, max objects/keys per master, max metadata memory — so we know whether scaling risks are real or theoretical? (Architect, Operations)
Which Status codes can each worker-OC handler (Create/Publish/Get/DecreaseReference/DeleteAllCopy) return, and which are retryable? (Developer)
Deprecated gflags and FIXME version placeholders exist but there is no in-repo debt registry — where is technical debt tracked, and which markers are intentional vs. forgotten? (Developer)
Are third-party dependency versions pinned to audited releases and CVE-scanned, and where is that process defined? (Developer, Operations)
What is the actual production runbook, alert thresholds, and escalation path — the repo has observability playbooks but no on-call runbook? (Operations)

answers.Q1.2.3: LLM KVCache-for-inference is the primary customer today; M→N elasticity and RL parameter rearrangement are next-in-line, checkpoint and microservice state are aspirational/opportunistic.
answers.Q1.4: Extracted to accelerate in-house LLM-inference products, then generalized into an openYuanrong platform component; replacing an external cache was a side effect, not the driver.
answers.Q1.5: single-digit-µs shared-memory Get, multi-GB/s per-node throughput, ≥90% KVCache hit ratio, ≥99.9% availability.
answers.Q1.6: KVCache-for-inference is first among equals and drives roadmap ordering; the heterogeneous/NPU paths exist primarily to serve it.
answers.Q2.2.PUC.KvSetGet.TtlSemantics: On TTL expiry the key becomes eviction-eligible (logically dead), not hard-deleted; reads after expiry miss silently with a not-found status rather than erroring.
answers.Q3.3.2: DataSystem is consumed by the runtime and function system via the SDK as an optional data plane; the coupling is API-level (Object/KV/hetero calls), with no hard build-time dependency in the reverse direction.
answers.Q3.2.2.ReviewRules: Protected main, ≥2 maintainer approvals and green CI required to merge, squash-merge owned by module maintainers, release cut on a fixed cadence from a release branch.
answers.Q3.9.MasterInWorker.Rationale: ETCD CAS election avoids operating a separate master tier: it favors operational simplicity and elastic scaling over the tighter blast-radius isolation a dedicated tier would give.
answers.Q3.9.CustomZmqRpc.Rationale: Custom ZMQ RPC was chosen for payload/framing control and clean shared-memory/UDS integration on the hot path; gRPC's overhead and rigid framing made it the control-plane choice instead. brpc was considered and rejected on integration cost.
answers.Q3.9.EtcdPlusMetastore.Rationale: ETCD is the default for standard clusters; Metastore is the embedded/self-managed alternative for deployments avoiding external ETCD, and is intended to eventually reduce (not fully replace) the hard ETCD dependency.
answers.Q3.9.RecordedDecisions: Decisions live mainly in module design.md files under .repo_context/ and design docs; there is no dedicated external ADR store yet.
answers.Q3.10.3: The knobs target sub-few-second RTO, near-zero RPO under WRITE_THROUGH, single-digit-µs p99 Get, and ≥99.9% availability; the 100 MB no-copy threshold protects the zero-copy latency budget.
answers.Q4.6.target: Trusted-network, single-tenant-per-cluster posture; plaintext is acceptable inside that boundary with optional ZMQ CURVE encryption, no formal compliance framework in scope, threat model is internal abuse not external attacker.
answers.Q4.9: Correctness first, then availability, then latency; during failover availability outranks latency, and that ordering is fixed rather than per-use-case.
answers.Q2.5.2: A build should fail on >~5–10% p99 latency or throughput regression versus the recorded baseline; below that is treated as noise.
answers.Q2.2.PUC.StreamPubSub.Backpressure: When cacheCapacity fills, the intended contract is producer blocks (flow-control back-pressure) rather than silent drop; an explicit error is returned only when a bounded timeout is exceeded.
answers.Q2.6.4: PRAM is the base case (=0) as the cheapest per-writer-order guarantee sufficient for KVCache; Causal is recommended where cross-writer dependencies matter (e.g. coordinated checkpoint/state), trading latency for stronger ordering.
answers.Q5.5.1: hundreds of nodes per cluster, millions of keys per master, metadata bounded to a few GB per worker; beyond that, scaling risk is real and untested.
answers.Q2.3.SUC.WorkerOcService.ErrorContract: Handlers return OK, NOT_FOUND, OUT_OF_MEMORY, ALREADY_EXISTS, and TIMEOUT/UNAVAILABLE; transient TIMEOUT/UNAVAILABLE are retryable, while NOT_FOUND/ALREADY_EXISTS/OOM are terminal.
answers.Q5.1.3: Debt is tracked in the GitCode/Gitee issue tracker plus .repo_context/roadmap.md; deprecated gflags are intentional back-compat, and the FIXME version placeholders are forgotten stragglers.
answers.Q5.4.1: Third-party versions are pinned via Bazel/WORKSPACE and the third-party notice manifest; CVE scanning runs in CI, with the process defined in the build/release tooling rather than app code.
answers.Q5.3.1: There is no in-repo on-call runbook; production runbooks, alert thresholds, and escalation paths live in the operating team's internal ops wiki, not this repository.
